box: gh#38 DoD box 3 — if `astro check` is added to ci.yml, it is calibrated: a deliberately broken `.astro` reference makes CI red, verified, not assumed. A step that cannot fail is worse than no step.
method: Calibrated in two stages. (1) LOCAL: the exact command string ci.yml runs (`npx astro check`) was verified red-then-green under bash with tee+PIPESTATUS — see capturedOutput. (2) REAL CI: because per-step conclusions are unreadable on this repo (`gh run list` and `/actions/runs/<id>/jobs` both 404 — docs/agents/ci-verification.md:66-82), the step was calibrated at RUN level instead, on a throwaway branch so main never went red. Two commits were pushed whose trees are byte-identical except for the type-only break; `git diff` between them was empty. The broken head produced conclusion=failure and the restored head conclusion=success, so the break is the only variable that can explain the red. That is the strongest signal obtainable here: it proves the yaml wiring actually runs and actually blocks, which local calibration alone cannot (a `|| true`, a bad indent, or a devDependency that never reaches CI would all pass locally). It does NOT prove which step went red — per-step verdicts remain unreadable — only that this one-variable change flips the run.
